author: Ranjith Shivahari
title: Offer or Just
simple_words: An offer can be accepted to make a contract. An invitation only asks people to make offers.

definitions.meaning: A person shows willingness to do or not do something, to get the other's assent. Acceptance of it creates a promise.
A step before the offer. It invites others to make offers, and cannot be accepted to form a contract.

key_points: An ==offer== is capable of acceptance; an invitation is not
Test: did the maker show intention to be bound on simple acceptance?
Display, catalogue, price list, tender notice, auction call = invitation
!!A general offer!! (reward advertisement) can be accepted by performing the condition

rows: Goods with price tag on display

insight.text: The customer's bid or request to buy is the offer; the seller's acceptance completes the contract.

memory_trick.explanation: A shop window, catalogue, tender notice or auctioneer's call only shows or invites. The bid or buyer's request is the offer; the reward ad is the exception.

steps: Is there intention to be bound?
Can simple acceptance close the deal?
Is it an advertisement for a reward?
Name it and cite the case
exam_tip: In MCQs, price tag, catalogue, tender notice and auction call mean invitation. A reward promise to anyone who performs means general offer.

doubt.question: Is a price-tagged item an offer by the shop?
doubt.answer: No. It is an invitation to offer. The customer offers by bringing it to the counter, and the shopkeeper accepts by taking the price.

mistakes_hook: don't fall for the price tag

mistakes.wrong: Goods with a price tag in a shop window are an offer
mistakes.right: They are an invitation to offer; the customer makes the offer
It is an invitation; the bidder's bid is the offer

mistakes.wrong: A tender notice is an offer to the bidders
mistakes.right: The notice invites tenders; each submitted tender is an offer

mistakes.wrong: A reward advertisement is only an invitation
mistakes.right: It is a general offer, accepted by performing the condition (Carlill case)
